---
title: Simple CNN on CIFAR10 dataset
description: Trains a simple deep CNN on the CIFAR10 small images dataset.
categories: [cv]
aliases:

---

Train a simple deep CNN on the CIFAR10 small images dataset.

It gets down to 0.65 test logloss in 25 epochs, and down to 0.55 after 50 epochs,
though it is still underfitting at that point.

If doing data augmentation you may try increasing the number of filters in convolutions
and in dense layers.

```{r}
library(keras3)



# Data Preparation --------------------------------------------------------

# CIFAR-10 is available in three sizes:
# - Full data: 50,000 training images and 10,000 test images
# - 50% data: a random subset with 25,000 training images and 5,000 test images
# - 25% data: a random subset with 12,500 training images and 2,500 test images

# The files are available in the course room in Lisam.

# Start with the 25% version to reduce memory use and training time.

path_cifar <- "cifar10_quarter.rds"

# Other available versions:
# path_cifar <- "cifar10_half.rds"
# path_cifar <- "cifar10_full.rds"

cifar10 <- readRDS(path_cifar)

# Feature scale RGB values in test and train inputs
x_train <- cifar10$train$x / 255
x_test <- cifar10$test$x / 255
y_train <- cifar10$train$y
y_test <- cifar10$test$y

# Parameters --------------------------------------------------------------

batch_size <- 32
epochs <- 10
data_augmentation <- FALSE


# Defining Model ----------------------------------------------------------

# Initialize sequential model
# images har size: 32*32 pixels, and 3 channels (color images)
model <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = c(32, 32, 3))

if (data_augmentation) {
  data_augmentation <- keras_model_sequential() %>%
    layer_random_flip("horizontal") %>%
    layer_random_rotation(0.2)

  model <- model %>%
    data_augmentation()
}

model <- model %>%
  # Start with hidden 2D convolutional layer being fed 32x32 pixel images
  layer_conv_2d(
    filters = 16, kernel_size = c(3, 3), padding = "same"
  ) %>%
  layer_activation_leaky_relu(negative_slope = 0.1) %>%

  # Second hidden layer
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 32, kernel_size = c(3, 3)) %>%
  layer_activation_leaky_relu(negative_slope = 0.1) %>%

  # Use max pooling
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2)) %>%
  layer_dropout(0.25) %>%

  # 2 additional hidden 2D convolutional layers
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 32, kernel_size = c(3, 3), padding = "same") %>%
  layer_activation_leaky_relu(negative_slope = 0.1) %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 64, kernel_size = c(3, 3)) %>%
  layer_activation_leaky_relu(negative_slope = 0.1) %>%

  # Use max pooling once more
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2)) %>%
  layer_dropout(0.25) %>%

  # Flatten max filtered output into feature vector
  # and feed into dense layer
  layer_flatten() %>%
  layer_dense(256) %>%
  layer_activation_leaky_relu(negative_slope = 0.1) %>%
  layer_dropout(0.5) %>%

  # Outputs from dense layer are projected onto 10 unit output layer
  layer_dense(10)

opt <- optimizer_adamax(learning_rate = learning_rate_schedule_exponential_decay(
  initial_learning_rate = 5e-3,
  decay_rate = 0.96,
  decay_steps = 1500,
  staircase = TRUE
))

model %>% compile(
  loss = loss_sparse_categorical_crossentropy(from_logits = TRUE),
  optimizer = opt,
  metrics = "accuracy"
)

# Training ----------------------------------------------------------------

model %>% fit(
  x_train, y_train,
  batch_size = batch_size,
  epochs = epochs,
  validation_data = list(x_test, y_test),
  shuffle = TRUE
)

model %>% evaluate(x_test, y_test)
```
